primary_task: Write a libFuzzer harness for a user's C/C++ target, build it with clang -fsanitize=fuzzer(,address), and run a fuzzing campaign.

requirements.name: clang/clang++ with libFuzzer (LLVM)
requirements.evidence: LLVM/Clang compiler (includes libFuzzer); `apt install clang llvm`
requirements.basis: bash: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, ...)

requirements.name: C/C++ target source
requirements.basis: grants: local_filesystem; target code presence not stated

requirements.name: downloads.sourceforge.net (libpng tarball, Example 1)
requirements.basis: lacks: network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy are open

requirements.name: raw.githubusercontent.com (harness, dictionary, FuzzedDataProvider)
requirements.basis: description: GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com) ... are open

requirements.name: long-running session and large virtual memory for ASan
requirements.evidence: Run for days/weeks, not minutes; Requires ~20TB virtual memory (disable memory limits: `-rss_limit_mb=0`)
requirements.basis: the manifest states no session duration or memory limits

notes: Core flow (apt install clang, build, run ./fuzz) works on Linux x86_64. The sourceforge download in the libpng worked example is blocked but is an example, not the core request (the libpng source is also on GitHub). Windows/macOS install sections are alternatives. If Example 1 were the task, the verdict would be BLOCKED unless the source is fetched from GitHub.
